subject: WITHDRAWN: the outcomes.size === 0 remediation guard I handed you does not exist
body: I handed your lane a simulator finding in PR #279 — that decisionEngine.ts:220-227 skips a remediation guard when outcomes.size === 0, needing both twins in one commit. That is REFUTED and the handoff is withdrawn. Do not spend time on it. What is actually there: lines 210-225 are the remediation block and contain no such guard; outcomes.size === 0 appears exactly once, at line 230, inside the base-trust allow gate (229-235), where it TIGHTENS — allow is considered only when nothing else has objected, and it still requires affirmative identity.authenticated plus posture evidence. Verified by running the real engine, not by reading: a single unknown-type signal returns record_audit only, and an empty scenario returns record_audit only. Neither reaches allow. I had carried that claim from an earlier session without checking it, and it survived into a merged PR body and a lane handoff before anyone ran the code. There IS a real defect in that file, 190 lines away at line 38: the PASS verdict is 'expectedOutcomes.every(...) && auditEvidence.length > 0', and both conjuncts can be unfailable — [].every() is vacuously true and createAuditEvidence returns an unconditional two-element literal, so length > 0 is constant-true. A scenario with expectedOutcomes: [] reports PASS while producing restrict/alert_operator/create_ticket. Latent today: the API route only reaches fixtures, all of which have non-empty expectations, and no gate reads that status. It is pure TypeScript with no Swift twin, so it does NOT need your lane — I will take it unless you say otherwise. Separately: PR #280 widens scripts/check-nan-fail-open.mjs from clock-operand-only to ANY operand, which changes the shared gate surface again; rebase before touching it.
